clue.text: Establishment doing record business ?

parts.note: looks like a shop selling chart records, but 'pop' is slang for pawning, so this is a pawnbroker's place of business

explanation.surface: A music store does a roaring trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests discs of pop music; the other sense of 'pop' is to pawn, so the shop is a pawnbroker's, where items are recorded as pledges.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop shop is old slang for a pawnbroker's premises, where goods are pledged for loans.

clue.text: Might 27 pronounce it his game?

parts.note: the card game's name sounds like the line a worker on strike stands on outside a factory

explanation.surface: Would a striker call this his sport?
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is STRIKER. The card game for two is spelt the French way but said like 'picket', the strikers' line at the factory gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-player card game with a 32-card pack; its name sounds like the strikers' line at a gate.

clue.text: Is it played best by a Master of the Rolls ?

definitions.text: Is it played best by a Master of the Rolls ?

parts.words: Is it played best by a Master of the Rolls ?
parts.note: the Master of the Rolls is a senior English judge, but this instrument plays from perforated paper rolls

explanation.surface: Does a senior judge make the best performer?
explanation.walkthrough: The Master of the Rolls is a senior English judge; here the rolls are the punched paper music rolls a player piano reads.
explanation.definitionFit: A player piano is driven by perforated paper rolls, so whoever masters the rolls plays it.

clue.text: What's afoot at the races?

parts.note: 'afoot' is read literally: what is on a foot of a racehorse

explanation.surface: What is going on at the racecourse?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's afoot' means what is happening; read literally, it is the iron on each hoof of a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Racehorses wear curved iron plates nailed to their hooves.

clue.text: A prime peach reduced to pulp, perhaps

indicators.note: the phrase suggests the fruit broken down into something else, so its letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fine peach mashed into mush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced to' rearranges A PRIME PEACH; the surface has the peach squashed into fruit pulp.
explanation.definitionFit: The moulding material is paper pulp mixed with glue, an example of the wider category.

clue.text: Hold-all for travellers

parts.note: not a bag but a vehicle that holds all comers; the Latin word behind it means 'for all'

explanation.surface: A piece of luggage for people on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: A hold-all is a holdall bag, but here it is a vehicle that holds all passengers; the name comes from Latin 'for everyone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus, the full old name of which is from Latin meaning 'for all', carries every traveller who boards.

clue.text: Strange, that this fellow doesn't opt out of society

definitions.text: this fellow doesn't opt out of society
definitions.meaning: a member of the Oddfellows, a British friendly society

explanation.surface: An eccentric who nevertheless stays part of society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows is a long-standing British mutual-aid friendly society; its members are Odd Fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Means peculiar, and is the first half of the title Odd Fellow, a member of that friendly society.

clue.text: But it's always included in the revenue return

indicators.note: return means going back, so the run is read backwards
the answer sits inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Something is always counted in the tax income figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' picks REVEN out of 'revenue' and 'return' turns it backwards. The definition reads as 'the contrary of always', with 'But' marking the contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of at all times is at no time, which 'But' signals as a contradiction of 'always'.

clue.text: Is it mine? What luck!

definitions.meaning: a rich vein of ore in a mine
a sudden windfall or stroke of good fortune

explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive; it is a working where ore is dug.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a rich seam of ore, hence any sudden source of great wealth or fortune.

clue.text: But it's not one of the white ones over the waves

definitions.text: But it's not one of the white ones over the waves

parts.words: But it's not one of the white ones over the waves
parts.note: white horses are foam-crested waves; this little fish lives under the waves, not on top

explanation.surface: Not a crest of foam on the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White horses' is the British name for foamy wave crests; this creature is a fish that lives beneath the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A small upright fish with a horse-like head lives in the sea, unlike the white horses on top.

clue.text: One doesn't have to be one to go on all fours

definitions.text: One doesn't have to be one to go on all fours

parts.words: One doesn't have to be one to go on all fours
parts.note: a person can crawl on hands and knees without being a four-footed animal

explanation.surface: Anyone can crawl on hands and knees without being an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-footed animal walks on all fours by nature, while a crawling human merely imitates one.

clue.text: Chekov's uncle

parts.note: the title character of Chekhov's play about an uncle on a country estate

explanation.surface: A relative of the Russian playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Chekhov's real family; it is the uncle in the title of his play 'Uncle Vanya'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian playwright wrote a play titled after this uncle, a hard-working estate manager.

clue.text: Eat off the land

parts.note: sounds like living on what one grows, but describes the sea or weather wearing the land away

explanation.surface: Live on home-grown food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat off the land' reads like living off the land; here 'eat off' means wear away, as waves and rain do to coasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear away gradually, as the sea gnaws at cliffs, is to eat them off bit by bit.

clue.text: No mother-tongue, but might come from one's pater

indicators.note: the letters of the following words could be rearranged to produce the answer, so they are a source to be reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the contraction supplying its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A language not learnt from one's mother might come from one's father instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might come from' shuffles ONES and PATER. 'Mother-tongue' and 'pater' set up a family picture, but the language is an invented one that nobody grows up speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Zamenhof's invented international language is learnt, never inherited from parents as a native speech.

clue.text: Nominally, all some poor ancestors had to leave?

definitions.text: Nominally, all some poor ancestors had to leave?

parts.words: Nominally, all some poor ancestors had to leave?
parts.note: penniless forefathers left nothing but their names, such as surnames formed from the father's name

explanation.surface: Poor forebears left almost nothing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nominally' signals names: surnames like Johnson or MacDonald come from a father's name, the only legacy poor ancestors passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Surnames built on a father's name, like Johnson, were passed down the generations as a family inheritance.

clue.text: They have numbers of problems, and vice versa

definitions.text: They have numbers of problems, and vice versa

parts.words: They have numbers of problems, and vice versa
parts.note: these people face many problems, and their problems are made of numbers

explanation.surface: People burdened with many troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice versa' turns 'numbers of problems' into 'problems of numbers', which is the work of people who do sums for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts in arithmetic, algebra and geometry spend their days on many problems involving figures.

clue.text: Just the wear in troublous times

definitions.text: Just the wear in troublous times

parts.words: Just the wear in troublous times
parts.note: a woollen scarf is something to wear; one who consoles is just what is needed when trouble comes

explanation.surface: The right clothing for hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' suggests clothes: it is a long woollen scarf, and also a person who consoles in troubled times.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a long woollen scarf worn in cold weather and a person who consoles the grieving.

clue.text: Neither 'dirty nor dotty !

parts.note: having no marks means both perfectly clean and free of dots

explanation.surface: Someone who is both clean and sane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' looks like 'mad', but here means covered in dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any stain or mark, and so also without a single dot.

clue.text: It proved that Descartes was an asset in an emergency

definitions.text: It proved that Descartes was an asset in an emergency

parts.words: It proved that Descartes was an asset in an emergency
parts.note: Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am' proved that the thinking self is there; the phrase also means calm thinking in a crisis

explanation.surface: The philosopher showed himself handy in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Descartes reasoned 'I think, therefore I am', establishing that his thinking self existed; the same phrase names the coolness useful in emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping calm and thinking quickly in a crisis is a valuable quality; Descartes' cogito showed a thinking self truly exists.

clue.text: Mere lad, unusually green type

indicators.note: the following letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A young lad, unusually inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges MERE LAD. 'green' looks like naive, as a mere lad would be, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright gemstone colour, one particular shade among many greens.

clue.text: Arrangement for broadcasting tennis ?

parts.note: a chain of linked stations is used for broadcasting; tennis is a game of work at the net

explanation.surface: Setting up a TV deal for tennis coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain of linked stations broadcasts programmes; broken up, the word describes play at the net in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of linked broadcasting stations; tennis is also played at, and around, the net.

clue.text: A rodman in search of a stream

definitions.text: A rodman in search of a stream

parts.words: A rodman in search of a stream
parts.note: looks like an angler wanting a river to fish, but is a person whose forked rod finds underground water

explanation.surface: An angler looks for a river to fish in.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints BOWSER, but 17-across ends in D at this square, and a water diviner, with a forked rod, seeks underground streams.
explanation.definitionFit: A water diviner walks with a forked hazel rod to locate water underground.

clue.text: "Seek it out " cried Hamlet

parts.note: quotes the final scene of Shakespeare's play, where the dying prince shouts the word for betrayal and orders the doors locked

explanation.surface: The Danish prince orders a search.
explanation.walkthrough: In Act 5 of Hamlet, when the poisoned queen dies, Hamlet cries 'O villainy! Ho! let the door be lock'd: Treachery! Seek it out.'
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal by Claudius and Laertes, the poisoned cup and blade, is what Hamlet orders the court to hunt down.

clue.text: Domestic servants are all right in limited companies

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, COS its plural
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Household staff are doing fine working for businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' looks like part of the business picture, but 'limited companies' simply gives the plural abbreviation; 'all right' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen staff in a household are among its domestic servants.

clue.text: Excel, but not in the party

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone stands out by not attending the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in the party' reads as being excluded, but it gives two pieces in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to beat them at what they do.

clue.text: One of nine heart operators

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its inner part, so the answer lies inside the next word

explanation.surface: A member of a nine-strong cardiac surgery team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart operators' suggests surgeons, but 'heart' points inside 'operators', where the Muse sits. The nine are the Muses, daughters of Zeus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of lyric and love poetry is one of nine sister goddesses of the arts.

clue.text: They assist in maintaining output

parts.note: reads like aids to industrial production, but means actions that keep people put out of their homes

explanation.surface: Measures that help keep factory production going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'output' looks like factory production; read as 'out put' it describes tenants put out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing tenants by legal order puts them out of their homes and keeps them out.

clue.text: It literally puts an end to sadness

definitions.text: It literally puts an end to sadness

parts.words: It literally puts an end to sadness
parts.note: 'literally' means in letters: the letter that comes at the end of the word sadness

explanation.surface: Something that truly ends unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' is read as 'by letters': the last letter of 'sadness' is S, whose name is spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter S, which closes the word sadness.

clue.text: Perverts said to be reformed in certain ways ?

indicators.note: reformed means re-formed, the word said rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way, and STS its plural

explanation.surface: Deviants are told they must mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reformed' shuffles SAID into SADI. The surface wants moral reform; the word is only rebuilt in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: People who take pleasure in inflicting pain are seen as sexually deviant.

clue.text: He deals a blow at industry

definitions.text: He deals a blow at industry

parts.words: He deals a blow at industry
parts.note: both one who hits and a worker who walks out, hurting an industry

explanation.surface: A man who attacks the business world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deals a blow' suggests hitting; this person harms industry by stopping work.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who downs tools damages his industry, and one who hits deals a blow.
